Remote reservoir in the upper Tywi valley behind the tallest dam in the UK (91 m), opened by Princess Alexandra on 15 May 1973. The name is a mapmaker's slip for Nant y Bryniau. Fanog farm was drowned, and its ruin reappears in droughts. Clay for the dam came from near Soar-y-Mynydd chapel. Dark Sky Discovery Site since 2019. Twm Siôn Cati's cave, the Cilycwm witch and the wizard of Cwrtycadno are all within 7 miles. The spillway roars after heavy rain.

A 19th-century hill farm in the upper Tywi, drowned when Llyn Brianne filled in 1972–73. Its ruin and roof show again when the reservoir is low, and it was once reachable on foot. Probably the farm in Ruth Bidgood's 1969 poem 'At Fanog'. Grid ref SN 80880 51230 (Powys side of the reservoir).

Hideout of the 'Welsh Robin Hood', Thomas Jones (c.1530–1609), on the wooded hill of the RSPB Gwenffrwd-Dinas reserve near Rhandirmwyn, just south of Llyn Brianne. Reached by the reserve's riverside trail and a scramble up the boulders. Position approximate.
